clue.text: Material males?

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A question about whether some fabric or substance is masculine.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'males' gives two male animals in turn; buckram is a stiff cloth used in bookbinding.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a coarse cloth stiffened with glue, used for bookbinding and hat shapes.

clue.text: Wager about the hazard of serving meat

indicators.note: the word for a wager goes around the word for danger

parts.note: a bet is a wager
a risk is a hazard

explanation.surface: Someone bets on the danger of dishing up meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef from the breast of the animal.

clue.text: Idle dreams of mediaeval dwellings in Iberia

parts.note: castles were fortified homes of the Middle Ages
Spain occupies most of the Iberian peninsula

explanation.surface: Fantasies about old fortresses on the peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means impractical daydreams or schemes with no hope of coming true.

clue.text: The government is to draw the line

definitions.meaning: control by a state, as in colonial administration
marking a straight line on paper with a ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both authority over a country and to mark a straight line with a ruler.

clue.text: Security services make a con cession for a refugee

parts.note: MI, Military Intelligence, as in MI5 and MI6, the British security services
a grant is something conceded or allowed

explanation.surface: Intelligence agents allow an exception for a displaced person.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is someone moving from their homeland, often fleeing hardship as a displaced person does.

clue.text: Time to seek a job

parts.note: to seek, as in seek advice, is to ask for it

explanation.surface: It is time to go looking for employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, a chore or assignment.

clue.text: Cricketing venue where Theodore meets Valerie

parts.note: Theo is the short form of the name Theodore
Val is the short form of the name Valerie

explanation.surface: Two friends with full names meet at a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground in Kennington, home of Surrey; 'meets' simply joins the two pet names.
explanation.definitionFit: This Kennington ground is one of England's main Test match stadiums for cricket.

clue.text: Benefit from taking Japanese wine

definitions.meaning: for the good of, as in 'for my benefit'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means behalf or advantage ('for his sake'), and also the fermented rice drink of Japan.

clue.text: The woman will get the account for the varnish

parts.note: she'll is the contraction of she will
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A woman receives the bill for some wood finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin from lac insects dissolved in alcohol to make a wood finish.

clue.text: What the ambitious astronaut aspires to do

definitions.text: What the ambitious astronaut aspires to do

parts.words: What the ambitious astronaut aspires to do
parts.note: the idiom for rising in status and success, taken literally as rising upward into space

explanation.surface: A spaceman's dream of making it big.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to rise in social or professional standing; an astronaut would literally ascend.

clue.text: Reading Plato in the original is quite beyond yours truly

definitions.text: Reading Plato in the original is quite beyond yours truly

parts.words: Reading Plato in the original is quite beyond yours truly
parts.note: the stock phrase for something incomprehensible, here taken literally: Plato wrote in ancient Greek, which the speaker cannot follow

explanation.surface: A confession that the classics in their own tongue defeat the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a thing is totally unintelligible, borrowed from the difficulty of the Hellenic language.

clue.text: The king takes beer and cabbage

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A monarch's dinner of ale and greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Kale is a leafy variety of cabbage with curly leaves.

clue.text: Cut right into the middle of the grotto

indicators.note: the letter for right goes into the centre of the word for the grotto

parts.note: a grotto is a small cave

explanation.surface: Someone slices straight into the heart of a cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut, as a joint of meat or a figure in stone.

clue.text: Appeal to father to get a large stone

parts.note: O is the exclamation of a plea or address, as in 'O Lord'
pa is an informal word for father
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A plea to dad for a big gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' is the vocative cry O, as in prayers; 'large stone' looks like one phrase but 'large' gives only L.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone with shifting rainbow colours.

clue.text: Do form a political organisation

definitions.meaning: a social gathering or celebration, as in 'a big do'
a group such as Labour or the Conservatives

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a festive gathering and a political group contesting elections.

clue.text: Refuse to fight

definitions.meaning: the noun, meaning rubbish or waste

explanation.definitionFit: The word means leftover waste to be thrown away, and also a minor brawl.

clue.text: Rehearsal of play which discriminated against Catholics

parts.note: a test run, like a rehearsal, is a trial before the real thing
to act is to play a part

explanation.surface: A trial run of a drama with an anti-Catholic message.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test Acts were English laws (1673 onward) barring Catholics and Nonconformists from public office unless they took Anglican communion.
explanation.definitionFit: This English statute required office-holders to take Anglican sacraments, so it excluded Roman Catholics.

clue.text: Brief study in secular accommodation

indicators.note: the word for study is placed inside the word for secular

parts.note: laic means lay or non-clerical, hence secular
to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A short spell of learning in non-religious lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like a noun or legal document but is the adjective; 'accommodation' just backs up 'in' as the housing signal. Con for study is an old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, like the terse Spartans of Laconia.

clue.text: The infant with very little spirit

parts.note: tiny means very little
a tot is a small measure of spirits such as rum

explanation.surface: A baby given a small drop of liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny tot is an affectionate phrase for a small child.

clue.text: A priest is made to do the rounds on foot

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new form, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A cleric is forced to walk his parish.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily from place to place.

clue.text: Everyone enters an examination to be top

indicators.note: the word for everyone goes inside the word for an exam

parts.note: a test is an examination
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The whole class sits an exam hoping to come first.
explanation.definitionFit: To be top in height is to be the highest of all, so the superlative of 'high-reaching' fits.

clue.text: Applaud a poor player in Len don

parts.note: to clap is to applaud
a ham is a bad, overacting performer

explanation.surface: An audience cheers a dreadful actor in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Clapham is a district of south London, famous from the phrase 'the man on the Clapham omnibus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapham is an area located within the British capital, south of the Thames.

clue.text: Fellow revolutionary is given protection

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a fellow or chap
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel comrade is granted a safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered is shielded or protected, as by insurance.

clue.text: The Scotsman looked wealthy

parts.note: mon is the Scots form of man
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A Scot appeared prosperous.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed means rich, having plenty of cash.

clue.text: A record's range

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A musician's vinyl album has a certain span.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' here is a mountain range, not the extent of a record.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain chain across Switzerland, France, Italy and Austria.

clue.text: Many are very partial to some garlic

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many
to love something is to be very partial to it

explanation.surface: Lots of people are fond of a bit of garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove is one segment of a garlic bulb.

clue.text: The bird was set loose before noon

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come ahead of the abbreviation for noon
letters that are set loose are freed to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird was released some time in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan is a large, long-necked water bird.

clue.text: Plucky poachers may profit by it

definitions.meaning: wild animals hunted for food, such as pheasant, which poachers take illegally

explanation.definitionFit: The word means courageous and up for anything, and also wild birds or animals hunted for sport or food.

clue.text: Hits back in the boxing-match

indicators.note: the word for hits is turned to read from right to left

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks or hits

explanation.surface: Someone strikes back during a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a practice bout of fighting with gloves.

clue.text: Tommy's estate belongs only to him

definitions.text: Tommy's estate belongs only to him

parts.words: Tommy's estate belongs only to him
parts.note: Tommy Atkins is slang for a British soldier of the lowest rank, so his possessions are a ranker's belongings; equally, land owned by one person and nobody else

explanation.surface: A man's land is his and nobody else's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tommy' is British slang for an ordinary soldier; read as a ranker's belongings, the phrase also means land not owned publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means land or possessions owned by an individual rather than the state, with a pun on the army rank.

clue.text: In France I get stumped by a joke

parts.note: je is French for I
ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A visitor in France is baffled by a gag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumped' is a cricket dismissal, abbreviated st on scorecards, not 'baffled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jest is a joke or witty remark.

clue.text: Free in deed, but treated with contempt

indicators.note: the word for free is put inside the word for an act

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
to rid is to free, as in rid of a burden

explanation.surface: Someone truly liberated, yet still scorned.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints the two words run together as 'indeed', which hides the container signal 'in'; 'Free' is the verb rid, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To be derided is to be mocked or scorned.
